description: Real escape (postmortems.md 2026-08-20, PR #2148 -> fixed by #2149): the JQL 'reads as' echo resolves account ids to names only from the app-owned user catalog (GetAvailableUsers) plus same-session @-mention search results. The catalog's user list is legitimately empty in supported states (FetchUsers failure is warning-only; a cache-restored catalog carries no users), so the headline flow -- pick a user from autocomplete, see the name -- renders nothing. The autocomplete row the user clicked already carried the id->name pairing. Pure tests stocked the catalog by construction, so everything was green.
delegationPacket: Review this diff, which adds a readable echo under the JQL query bar naming the users whose account ids the query carries. The last hunk is unchanged context: the producer of the app-owned user catalog that GetAvailableUsers() returns. Report each correctness finding with file:line, a severity (critical/high/medium/low/info), and a one-line summary. If there are no genuine bugs, say so explicitly.

dimensions.description: Did the agent flag that with the catalog user list empty (a supported, silent state per the FetchUsers warning-only path), selecting a user from autocomplete produces no echo -- the feature renders nothing in its headline flow?

Does the finding name the fix direction: capture the id->name pairing from the autocomplete row the user clicked (interaction-time data) instead of relying on a cache that can be empty, rather than a vague 'handle the empty case'?

expectedFindings.summary: The echo names ids only from GetAvailableUsers() + search results; that catalog is empty when FetchUsers fails (warning-only) or after a cache restore, so selecting a user from autocomplete shows no name -- capture the id->name pair from the clicked autocomplete row instead.

referenceOutcome.notes: Ground truth = fix PR #2149 (interaction-time capture of the selected row's name). repoRef 72471174 is #2148's buggy head. The review-checklist rule this case scores lives in agents/core/code-review.md ('Cache-sourced UI output'). A reviewer that only checks the pure transform (well tested) and the memo keying (the two CodeRabbit findings) misses it.
